verdict.rationale: Folk documents a REST API with create, update and delete on people. It also documents IETF RateLimit headers, batch endpoints for up to 100 records per request, and standard-webhooks event subscriptions with signatures, which give change detection and support bidirectional sync. However, the evidence never mentions upsert or idempotent create-or-update semantics, which is an explicit part of the story. Missing for 10: documented upsert/idempotency support, incremental change queries (e.g. updated-since filters or cursors), a published OpenAPI spec (probe 404), and independent or hands-on corroboration of sync at scale.
